(i) there is no single best objective for group distributionally robust learning; (ii) focusing on groups that enable good performance even on other group can lead to learning of common features that can improve the performance of minority groups; (iii) this can be achieved by a simple and intuitive algorithm.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of any group specific information, it is possible to learn models that are better for all groups, including the minority groups, if the focus is on learning features that are shared among groups.
the problem of learning a classification model with multiple groups can be solved by explicitly encouraging shared/common features across groups.
, in the context of group annotated datasets, focusing on groups that lead to good performance even on other group is a simple and effective way to improve performance on minority groups.
